subject: Account decommission timeline & log retention questions
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@corestream.com>, Tim O'Leary <tim@corestream.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Account decommission timeline & log retention questions

Hi Sarah / Tim —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarifying questions so we can scope an accurate SOW and timeline for CoreStream's exit path. High-level takeaways: you want predictable finalization of customer data after contract termination, an auditable trail proving removal, and clear constraints around backups and snapshots.

Questions / assumptions for confirmation:
1) Scope: Confirm the data sets you want included in the finalization (chat transcripts, embeddings, metadata, usage logs).
2) Residency: CoreStream production is in us-west with optional eu copies for reporting — confirm whether eu-copies must be wiped or retained for legal reasons.
3) Finalization window: You indicated a 30-day business window for primary data removal + 90-day retention for backups — is that a hard SLA requirement or a starting point?
4) Backups & snapshots: Our platform currently overwrites incremental snapshots after 90 days. We need to confirm whether CoreStream requires explicit overwrite or exclusion from backup retention (which may extend timeline).
5) Audit evidence: CoreStream asked for an attestation and access to redacted audit logs showing deletion events. Do you need a signed attestation (PDF) or is an API-delivered audit export sufficient?
6) KMS / key handback: If CoreStream uses their own KMS, confirm if you expect a key revocation-based irrevocable wipe or assisted key handback.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi and Marcus to provide a short playbook that covers: deletion steps, backup handling, and what proof we can deliver (attestation + audit export).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to confirm technical constraints (snapshots, cross-region replication).
- CoreStream to confirm the exact object classes in scope.

I've attached a one-page data-handling summary and a sample playbook that outlines standard Redwood finalization mechanics.

If you can reply with the answers inline, we'll convert this into a mutual action plan and a draft SOW.

Thanks —

Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (summary PDF), sample-decommission-playbook.docx (playbook template)

From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@corestream.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim O'Leary <tim@corestream.com>, CoreStream Legal <legal@corestream.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account decommission timeline & log retention questions

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is helpful. Quick responses inline: 
1) Scope: Include customer conversation logs, parsed embeddings, user IDs and associated metadata (we do NOT need low-level system telemetry like host-level metrics).
2) Residency: Primary data is only in us-west; we have a reporting replica in eu-central used for analytics. Legal flagged that EU copies must be treated the same unless we get explicit confirmation otherwise — for now, plan to remove both.
3) Finalization window: 30 business days for primary deletion is our internal target. We're open to discussing exceptions for backups but need a maximum cap (ideally 120 days total from request).
4) Backups & snapshots: We need clarity if Redwood can selectively exclude snapshots that contain CoreStream PII or if the process is a time-based overwrite only. If it's time-based only, we need a guaranteed maximum time to final overwrite.
5) Audit evidence: We need a signed attestation and a machine-readable audit export (CSV/JSON) showing deletion events and timestamps. CoreStream Legal copied here — they'd like to review the attestation template.
6) KMS: We use our own KMS for customer encryption. We'd prefer a key-revocation approach if that yields immediate practicality. If there are limitations, state them.

Can Rishi / Marcus provide the attestation template and the technical steps? Also please confirm if there are any costs associated with expedited deletion of backup snapshots. We'll aim for the deep-dive on Tue 3 Apr if that works for your team.

– Sarah
Sarah Jensen
Head of Platform Operations | CoreStream
sarah.jensen@corestream.com

Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account decommission timeline & log retention questions

Stephanie / team —

Looping in legal and infra for the specifics. Quick notes from the infra side:
- Primary deletion: we can purge account-level objects and associated KV caches within 48–72 hours of an approved request for active datastores. The orchestration will emit a deletion event with a UUID that can be included in the audit export.
- Backups/snapshots: currently snapshot retention is time-based; we can offer an expedited rewrite policy but it requires a short maintenance window and is billable (expedited purge fee applies). Standard overwrite occurs at the configured retention boundary (typically 90 days).
- KMS: If CoreStream manages keys externally (BYOK) we can coordinate revocation handoff; revocation will render stored encrypted blobs unreadable but does not remove the physical bytes from snapshots — we can document that as an acceptable mitigation if CoreStream signs off.

From Legal (Laura):
- We'll attach a deletion attestation template for review. It includes: scope, timestamped event IDs, responsible operator identity, and statement of retention exceptions (if any). We can provide a signed PDF and a machine-readable export.

I'll attach two artifacts: the one-page attestation draft and the technical playbook that details the steps, event IDs, and expected timelines.

Action items:
- Stephanie: send CoreStream the attestation + playbook (attached).
- Marcus: please confirm expected maintenance windows and rough cost for expedited snapshot rewriting.
- CoreStream: confirm final scope list and whether key-revocation alone suffices for you.

Rishi
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf, sample-decommission-playbook.docx

Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account decommission timeline & log retention questions

Sarah / Tim —

Thanks — attaching the attestation draft and playbook per Rishi/Laura. High-level proposal for the MLP (minimal launch plan):
- Scope confirmed: conversation logs, embeddings, user IDs, metadata.
- Primary purge: 30 business days target; we can commit to a hard cap of 45 business days for covered objects (subject to SOW).
- Backups: standard overwrite at 90 days; option for expedited rewrite to shorten to 14 days post-request (expedited fee applies).
- Evidence: signed attestation PDF + machine-readable audit export (JSON) with deletion event IDs.
- KMS: if CoreStream revokes BYOK keys we will mark blobs as unreadable; we'll still include the deletion events in the audit.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sarah to confirm scope and approve the attestation template (legal OK).
2) I will book a 60-minute technical deep-dive Tue 3 Apr 11:00am PT (invite sent).
3) Marcus to follow up after the deep-dive with an expedited rewrite estimate if you want the 14-day option.

If that reads OK I will turn this into a short mutual action plan and attach the SOW draft for timeline + pricing.

Best,
Stephanie
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
